column1: # The checks of shell/secure-boot-modes.nsh, the boot of shell-secure-boot-modes-setup and
# shell-secure-boot-modes-user: variable set refuses AuditMode and DeployedMode without their
# flags, naming them, and with them names the absent mode variables; PK and every other global

column3: . == {"error_message": "variable set writes AuditMode only with --enter-audit-mode-clearing-pk, in the UEFI Shell: \"Entering Audit Mode has the side effect of changing SetupMode == 1, PK is cleared, and the new DeployedMode == 0\" (UEFI 2.11 section 32.3.3)"}
. == {"error_message": "AuditMode and DeployedMode are absent, which UEFI 2.11 sections 3.3 and 32.3 define for the Secure Boot modes, so the firmware tells no mode to check the transition against"}

. == {"error_message": "variable set writes DeployedMode only with --enter-deployed-mode-irreversibly, in the UEFI Shell: \"to move from Deployed Mode to any other mode requires a secure platform-specific method, or deleting the PK, which is authenticated\" (UEFI 2.11 section 32.3)"}
. == {"error_message": "AuditMode and DeployedMode are absent, which UEFI 2.11 sections 3.3 and 32.3 define for the Secure Boot modes, so the firmware tells no mode to check the transition against"}
